To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Membrane tethered TRPducin peptides patterned after a highly conserved protein domain in the C termini of all TRP channels selectively inhibit TRPV channel activity in vitro and in intact cells, without significantly affecting other ion channels or receptors, or the capsaicino sensitivity of TRPV1 channel, and that TRPducins block all modes of TRV1 channel activity, including heat and capsaicin, in rat primary sensory neurons in vivo.
We have developed a novel molecular strategy to generate TRPV1 antagonism based on peptides that are anchored to the membrane via a palmitoyl chain and patterned after the C terminus TRP domain.
we have discovered a novel family of peptides that are able to block TRPV1 channels with micromolar potency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular and physiological mechanisms underlying the sensation of pain, with a particular emphasis on the role of TRPV1 and TRPA1 ion channels.
the molecular mechanisms of TRP channels, in particular the TRPV1 receptor, which has been implicated in diverse physiological processes and in the pathology of inflammatory and neuropathic pain.
the development of novel TRPV1 antagonistic molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TRP p5 peptide selectively inhibits TRPV1 channels in a non-competitive manner.
TRPducins are noncompetitive, sequence specific, voltage independent TRPV1 blockers that may be exploited to generate novel molecular tools for studying the TRP super family of ion channels.
TRP p5 is a non-competitive TRPV1 blocker that acts on the TRP domain, and is therefore a TRPducin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a novel class of TRPV1 channel blockers that are non competitive, voltage independent and sequence specific.
we have identified and characterized a novel class of TRPV1 blockers that are noncompetitive, sequence specific, voltage independent, and that can be exploited for the treatment of pain.
we developed a new class of TRPV1 antagonistic compounds that are based on a sequence of 15 amino acids that is conserved in the C termini of all members of the TRP channel family.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TRPducins represent a new molecular strategy for the development of selective pharmacological tools for the study of TRP channels.
we have identified the C-terminal domain of the TRPV1 channel as a potential target for the development of novel pharmacological tools.
TRPducins are the first example of a new class of TRP channel blockers.
